capitals.name: Lobamba (royal and legislative capital; Mbabane is the executive capital)
capitals.note: The Eswatini page names Mbabane executive and Lobamba legislative capital and dates neither; History of Eswatini gives Zombodze for Sobhuza I (d. 1815) and Hhohho for Mswati II (from 1839). One entry bridges the whole life (confidence low); the two towns are 15 km apart.

keyframe_review.note: 17,181 km2 for 1885-1894, 0.99 of today's 17,364 km2 (infobox, undated). Swazi independence was recognised by the British in 1881 and in the London Convention of 1884 (article XII); Mswati II had 'greatly extended the area of the country to twice its current size' in the 19th century, so the shape is the post-conquest core. Cliopatria begins the row in 1885 although the kingdom dates from the mid-18th century under Ngwane III.

correction.text: Swaziland as Cliopatria draws it for 1885-1894 (17,181 km2)

keyframe_review.note: New keyframe for 1895-1899: Cliopatria has no Swaziland row for these years and folds the country into its South African Republic shape (direct territory). 'In 1894, a convention placed Swaziland under the South African Republic as a protectorate'; the Republic administered it until the Second Boer War (October 1899). The outline is the 1885 one, drawn as a vassal of the South African Republic (events of 1894 and 1899).

17,048 km2 for 1900-1904: unchanged outline. After the British victory in the Second Boer War, Swaziland became a British High Commission Territory in 1903 (History of Eswatini: 'a British protectorate'); the status change is in the ledger.

17,048 km2 for 1905-1907, the same outline. The 1904 Swaziland Administration Proclamation set up a commission on the concessions and in 1907 ... Swazi land was partitioned (carried out in 1909; 38% set aside for the Swazi): land ownership, not the country's border.

correction.text: the Swazi kingdom within its present boundaries, a British protectorate until 1968

keyframe_review.note: New keyframe for 1908-1968, years Cliopatria leaves out (its British Africa shape holds the country, which was a High Commission Territory/protectorate from 1903 to independence on 6 September 1968): the outline of the 1900-1907 and 1969 shapes, which differ by 0.5%. The pages opened do not mention any boundary change in 1903-1968 (confidence 1 for the bridge).
17,129 km2 for 1969-1972: 'regained its full independence on 6 September 1968' and became the Kingdom of Swaziland. Infobox 17,364 km2: ratio 0.99.

17,289 km2 for 1973-1975: identical to the 1976 shape at the gazetteer's resolution (the 160 km2 difference is vertex noise, no cell differs). 12 April 1973: Sobhuza II annulled the 1968 constitution by decree, a constitutional, not a territorial, event.
17,129 km2 for 1976-2023, the independent kingdom; renamed Kingdom of Eswatini on 19 April 2018 (announced by Mswati III).

region.text: Swaziland as Cliopatria draws it for 1885-1894 (17,181 km2)

ledger.note: 1885: Cliopatria's Swaziland row begins; the kingdom itself is older. 'The Swazis established their kingdom in the mid-18th century under the leadership of Ngwane III'; Sobhuza I consolidated it (king in 1815), Mswati II succeeded in 1839 and Mbandzeni was chosen after 1872; British recognition of Swazi independence came in 1881 and the London Convention of 1884. 1885 is the first year of Cliopatria's shape, not a founding.

region.text: Swaziland as Cliopatria draws it for 1885-1894 (17,181 km2)

ledger.note: 1894: Swaziland becomes a South African Republic protectorate. 'In 1894, a convention placed Swaziland under the South African Republic as a protectorate' (History of Eswatini: the Swazi proclamation supporting it was 'signed by the Queen Regent and Swazi Council in December 1894', Ngwane V crowned in 1895, the Republic's administration under Krogh lasting to 1899). The south-african-republic dossier records the same relation.

region.text: Swaziland as Cliopatria draws it for 1885-1894 (17,181 km2)

ledger.note: October 1899: the South African Republic's protectorate lapses. The arrangement continued 'until the outbreak of the Second Boer War in October 1899'; Ngwane V (Bhunu) died on 10 December 1899 and his mother Labotsibeni became regent (History of Eswatini).

region.text: Swaziland as Cliopatria draws it for 1900-1904 (17,048 km2)

ledger.note: 1903: Britain takes Swaziland. After the British victory in the Second Boer War, Swaziland became a British High Commission Territory, but 'a protectorate was not established because terms had not been agreed' with the Queen Regent; History of Eswatini says In 1903 ... Swaziland became a British protectorate. The year is agreed, the label is not (confidence 2); administered from South Africa until the Transvaal's self-government in 1906.

region.text: Eswatini as Cliopatria draws it for 1969-1972 (17,129 km2)

ledger.note: 6 September 1968: Swaziland regains independence. Eswatini regained its full independence on 6 September 1968 (History of Eswatini: 'and became the Kingdom of Swaziland'); United Nations membership 24 September 1968.
19 April 2018: the Kingdom of Eswatini. 'On 19 April 2018, Mswati III announced the country's renaming to Kingdom of Eswatini.' Colour and dossier continue.

wars.name: Second Boer War (Swaziland)
wars.outcome: Swaziland was indirectly involved: British forces operated there and the Boers were expelled by February 1902; the South African Republic's protectorate ended in October 1899 and Britain took over in 1903.
wars.note: No border moved and no zone is contested.

certainty.note: The pages give no boundary description (not even for the 1881 and 1884 conventions that recognised Swazi independence); Cliopatria's outline is the modern country's, drawn back through the protectorate years.
The independent kingdom keeps the colonial boundary; the pages give no change.

notes: ONE STATE, TWO CLIOPATRIA ROWS: 'Swaziland' (1885-1907) and 'Eswatini' (1969-2024) share Wikidata Q1050 and are the same Swazi monarchy (Ngwenyama and the Queen Mother, regency of Labotsibeni 1899-1921, independence 1968), cut by Cliopatria's gap 1908-1968 when the country was a British High Commission Territory/protectorate and its outline sits inside the 'British Africa' shape. Written as one dossier under the earlier slug with both Names, as the brief instructs; af-08-l (which owns the eswatini row in the brief) should not write a second dossier, only add the post-1968 history if it has pages for it (the 1969-2024 shapes are reviewed here from the Eswatini page alone: no events after 1968 except the 2018 renaming). Two pages opened (budget 1-2 for 3 shapes; the 5 later shapes were reviewed on the same two pages). NOT SETTLED: (1) The kingdom's earlier history: founded in the mid-18th century (Ngwane III), consolidated by Sobhuza I (1815), enlarged by Mswati II 'to twice its current size' (1839-1865), land deeds of 1846 and 1855 to the Dutch republics, the South African Republic's 1868 annexation proclamation: a pre-1885 'swazi-kingdom' dossier (af-07-x?) is needed, and this dossier's 'found' event at 1885 is confidence 1 and marks only the start of Cliopatria's shape. (2) The 1881 Pretoria Convention and 1884 London Convention are on both pages, but no boundary terms; so the 1885 outline is not tested. (3) The status 1903-1968: pages disagree (High Commission Territory per the Eswatini page, 'British protectorate' per History of Eswatini); drawn as a British vassal (protectorate tint), the keyframe 1908-1968 bridges the outline at confidence 1. (4) The 1890 'triumviral administration' (British, the Dutch republics and the Swazi) and the 18 December 1889 provisional council after Mbandzeni's death, the 1890-1894 conventions, and the 1904-1909 land partition (38% of the country set aside for the Swazi by 1910) change who administers or owns land, not the border: no events. (5) No ruler strip: only partial dates are on the pages (Mswati II from 1839 to 1865, regency of Tsandzile Ndwandwe to 1875, Mbandzeni died 1889, Bhunu crowned 1895 and died 10 December 1899, Sobhuza II from 1921). (6) Capital: one bridged entry, as the pages do not date Mbabane or Lobamba. (7) Slugs: 'eswatini' (1969-2024) would be redundant; the colour agent should seed one colour for slug swaziland. Gazetteer: none needed (all regions are Cliopatria shapes).
